full_judgment: 28. The learned Additional Attorney General has lastly contended that when the property has already been vested in the Government, it cannot be divested by sale or otherwise and consequently the decree for sale of the land cannot be executed. The learned Additional Attorney General has however failed to cite any law which prohibits disposal by transfer of any property vested in the Government. The property being vested in the Government, their authority to deal with it has been rather strengthened. It may be mentioned here that with the abolition of all rent-receiving interests in land under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, all land vested in the Government who thereby got absolute power to dispose of land in any manner, such as sale, lease settlement. The contention of the learned Additional Attorney General that a vested property cannot be disposed of by sale has got no substance. We therefore upheld the contention of Mr Paul that with the repeal of Defence of Pakistan Rules, the Administration and Disposal Order made thereunder also stood repealed. The bar to the execution of the decree passed in favour of the appellant, I find, has been removed. The decree is found to be quite executable. In the result, the appeal is allowed and the impugned order of the High Court Division along with the order of the Executing Court is set aside and it is directed that the Execution Case No. 4 of 1967 be disposed of in the light of this judgment. No order as to cost.
